items.title: New agent framework facilitates biological database retrieval and integration
items.summary: Biological research questions often span multiple bioinformatics databases, which differ in data structures, access interfaces and coverage. To retrieve and integrate data across databases, researchers need to select suitable sources and call the corresponding query interfaces.

items.summary: People may have been getting high off cannabis earlier than previously thought—at least 2,800 years ago, a new study suggests.

items.title: Yale scientists may have found a shortcut to the anti-aging benefits of eating less
items.summary: Yale researchers have discovered that moderate calorie restriction reduces an immune protein linked to aging and chronic inflammation, apparently independently of weight loss. Blocking this protein could potentially mimic some of the benefits of eating less and help people stay healthier for longer.

items.title: MIT scientists discover a hidden switch that helps colon cancer spread
items.summary: Scientists have discovered a hidden biological pathway that allows colon cancer to spread and found that a high-fat diet can amplify its activity in mice. Blocking this pathway could offer a powerful new strategy for preventing potentially deadly metastasis.

items.title: New cancer drug tears down tumors’ walls and unleashes the immune system

items.title: Why squeezing a rock can pull it apart
items.summary: When a brittle material, such as a ceramic, rock or concrete sample, is squeezed between two plates, it can split lengthwise, even if the plates are pushing its ends together. So far, the physical explanation for this phenomenon has remained largely unclear.

items.title: Sleeping 9 hours a night after 50 may be a surprising warning sign
items.summary: A large Finnish study suggests that how well and how long you sleep after age 50 may influence the length of your working career. Both severely disrupted sleep and sleeping nine or more hours a night were associated with spending less time in the workforce.
